Declare the design of a pollination experiment

Source: R/design.R
pollin_design.Rd

Names the role of each treatment level (the arms) and the layout of the experiment. The layout fixes the random structure used when models are fitted: one random intercept for each level of the unit nesting declared in pollin_data(), outer to inner, with an optional random treatment slope on one unit level, giving a pollination effect that varies between those units.

Usage

pollin_design(x, arms, layout, reference = "open", slope = NULL)

Arguments

x

A pollin_data() object.

arms

Named character vector mapping arm roles to treatment levels, for example c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"). Roles are "excluded", "open" and "supplemented"; every treatment level must be mapped.

layout

One of "crd", "rcbd", "split_plot", "matched_pairs" or "multi_site". There is no default.

reference

The arm that dependence is measured against: "open" (the default) or "supplemented". It must be one of the declared arms.

slope

The unit level carrying a random treatment slope. NULL (the default) uses the layout's default from the table above; FALSE fits no slope; a column name from the unit nesting puts the slope there.

Value

An object of class pollin_design: a list holding the pollin_data() object data, arms, layout, reference, slope and the random-effect terms random.

Details

LayoutUnits, outer to innerTreatment variesDefault slope
"crd"experimental unit (and subsamples within it)between unitsnone
"rcbd"block, then any inner levelswithin blocksnone
"split_plot"block, whole plot, then any inner levelswithin whole plotsnone
"matched_pairs"any outer levels, then the pairwithin pairsnone
"multi_site"site, then any inner levelswithin sitessite

In a split-plot layout the pollination treatment is taken to be the sub-plot factor (for example cages within variety plots). The design checks that every arm appears in every block, whole plot, pair or site, and warns with a count when it does not.

Examples

df <- data.frame(
  pods = rpois(48, 30),
  trt = rep(c("Cage", "Open"), 24),
  Site = rep(letters[1:4], each = 12),
  Plot = rep(rep(c("p1", "p2"), each = 6), 4)
)
pd <- pollin_data(df, "pods", "trt", unit = c("Site", "Plot"))
pollin_design(pd, arms = c(excluded = "Cage", open = "Open"),
              layout = "multi_site")
#> <pollin_design>
#>   layout    : multi_site 
#>   arms      : excluded = Cage, open = Open 
#>   reference : open 
#>   units     : Site / Plot 
#>   random    : (trt | Site) + (1 | Site:Plot)
